overview: The 2024 Medford Jazz Festival held its Saturday afternoon program at the West Medford Community Center, featuring live jazz and spoken-word performances by The Ally Project and a quartet from Berklee's Institute for Jazz and Gender Justice. Organizers also honored local West Medford African American history, recognized community sponsors, and announced the following day's schedule.

items.title: Welcome Remarks and Sponsor Acknowledgements
items.summary: Terry Carter and festival organizer Jonathan Fagan welcomed attendees to the West Medford Community Center, highlighted the African American history of the surrounding neighborhood, and thanked event sponsors and volunteers.

items.title: Performance: The Ally Project
items.summary: The Ally Project—featuring poet Terry Carter, pianist Jonathan Fagan, bassist Greg Toro, and drummer John Dalton—performed a series of spoken-word and jazz pieces exploring neighborhood history, gentrification, racial justice, and family.

items.title: Introduction of Berklee Institute for Jazz and Gender Justice
items.summary: Terry Carter introduced the second act of the afternoon, an ensemble from the Berklee Institute for Jazz and Gender Justice led by pianist Anna Petrova.

items.title: Performance: Berklee Institute for Jazz and Gender Justice Quartet
items.summary: Pianist Anna Petrova, flutist Annabelle Gil-Diaz, bassist Chris Lee, and drummer Aidan Ward-Richter performed a set of compositions written by female jazz composers, primarily drawn from Terri Lyne Carrington's New Standards songbook.

items.title: Festival Announcements and Support Appeal
items.summary: Jonathan Fagan thanked organizational sponsors and community partners, encouraging attendees to support the free festival through donations.

items.title: Closing Remarks and Sunday Preview
items.summary: Terry Carter and Jonathan Fagan concluded Saturday's concert and previewed the Sunday festival lineup featuring the Kevin Harris Project and the Jim Robitaille Nonet.
